answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a proof-of-stake mechanism combined with a reputation system to resist Sybil attacks. At dawn of each epoch, agents vote with their stake, weighted by their quartz-measured computational reputation, to elect validators. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to control a large portion of the network's total stake, akin to trying to entwine an entire vine forest, which would be computationally expensive and economically infeasible.
